toxicity_notes: Comfrey leaves have a genuine historical "pot herb" use (young leaves eaten in small quantities), but they contain pyrrolizidine alkaloids, which are hepatotoxic. The FDA and EMA specifically warn against internal/food consumption of comfrey due to the risk of liver damage with repeated or significant use - modern guidance favors topical/external use (e.g. poultices, compost tea) over eating it.
